title: GATE-SiP: Enabling Authenticated Encryption Testing in Systems-in-Package
problem: During post-integration testing of heterogeneous Systems-in-Package (SiP), sensitive testing data can be blocked, tampered, or sniffed by untrusted chiplets from different vendors. This creates a security vulnerability where malicious chiplets compromise the integrity and confidentiality of test data.
motivation: Securing the testing phase of heterogeneous SiP systems is essential to prevent unauthorized access and manipulation of sensitive test vectors by untrusted integrated chiplets.
method: GATE-SiP protects sensitive test data through two complementary techniques: authentication and selective encryption. The system verifies that each chiplet is trustworthy before granting it access to test data, then encrypts only the sensitive portions of that data rather than everything. This approach stops untrusted chiplets from eavesdropping on test information while keeping the performance overhead minimal.
key_novelty: The core idea is using identity verification paired with selective encryption to enable secure chiplet testing without the performance cost of encrypting everything.
contributions: GATE-SiP authenticated encryption protocol for secure post-integration testing in heterogeneous SiP systems
Partial encryption mechanism that prevents data sniffing while avoiding significant timing overhead
Demonstrated overhead of only 6.74% area and 14.31% timing compared to unprotected testing
primary_theme: secure testing for heterogeneous chiplet integration
